events.title: Power-up system: enemies now drop more than just XP
events.summary: The first demo players noticed that enemies only drop XP. At first I thought that was enough, but if you ask, how can I say no? :) Now they drop power-ups too. A power-up stays on the ground for 20 seconds and gives a short but noticeable effect. Where they come from Elites drop one power-up, bosses drop two. events.title: The story is finally done!!! Do you like Disco Elysium?
events.summary: For almost a month I worked on the story and nothing but the story, and I can finally say it's done. The story used to be there just to tick a box. It ran along a single line: read, click, drive on. Now it's built from separate scenes. Each one has a moment where the decision is yours. Who to take into the convoy, who to make a deal with, and who to fight. {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46020580/21cc5d8123adc16a7014d55056590eb8b3bcfc16.png Choices don't just change a line of dialogue. events.title: The toxic cloud is no longer a green filter
events.summary: The toxic cloud rework is finally done. You can see the difference here: I didn't quite reach the look I had in my head, unfortunately. The result is still good. The part I enjoy most is mixing the toxic cloud with the swarm. Luring the mindless things in and watching them go is real fun. What I can't work out is how to build that into the gameplay. Anyone got ideas? A wagon with toxin? Or gas traps out on the map?

events.title: The asphalt cracks for real now
events.summary: Small update — but you can see it. Cracks Reworked the road decay effect. Cracks used to spread across the ground as pale smudges; now the asphalt itself splits — the fractures open up around the locomotive and stay behind you. Driving over them is still a bad idea: the convoy bogs down and loses speed. events.title: My name is Legion — enemies now come in the thousands
events.summary: So, now that the visuals are more or less sorted out, it is time to add some action. This is a bullet heaven after all: you need to shoot a lot, and for that you need a lot of enemies. I mean, a couple of dozen mobs — hardly the end of the world, right? A couple of thousand, now that is impressive. That is exactly why I am not moving to 3D: so I can throw thousands of enemies at you even on weak machines.The hordeThis is the big one. events.title: Nobody asked, but I redrew the wasteland
events.summary: Honestly, the visuals were fine. The road read clearly, enemies stood out, resources didn't look like debris — functionally everything worked. It just wasn't anything to look at.And I wanted it to be. I wanted the frame to be worth something on its own: for the wasteland to feel like a place you're actually driving through, not a backdrop a train sprite slides across. events.title: The Rescued Get to Work
events.summary: Why The story is about rescuing people, and the whole meta layer was built around that: the base, the foremen, the buildings. But in the run itself the rescued didn't take part at all — you pulled someone out of a shelter, and until the base they just rode in the locomotive. I wanted them to matter right away, not only in the base window. Crew Now the rescued work right in the run. A person climbs out of the shelter, takes a post along the locomotive and gets to work. Every captured invasion point now greets you with a full-screen splash: the defeated boss on the ruins of its lair, the war progress, and what you earned on this faction’s soil — sectors cleared, people rescued, blueprints recovered.Campaign finale. events.title: The game is ready for Early Access
events.summary: A surprising thing happened today. After three months of hard work, I looked at the game and realized: it's ready for Early Access. There's nothing big left on the list — only polishing and balancing what's already there.What that means in practice:— All four factions are finished. events.summary: Last time I promised the next post would be about the radio tower and quests. Keeping my word: it's all in the demo now. events.title: Demo's out: we're rolling toward release
events.summary: The Last Convoy demo is live on Steam — free, no sign-up, no strings attached. In short: a survivors-like where, instead of a character, you've got a growing road train. We drive through a dying world, and every car you hook on adds a gun or some function. The longer the train, the stronger you are — and the clumsier.
